title: Management Summary — Verdict fragment
description: Structured Management Summary verdict. The generator and gate share the concern rating; the LLM authors evidence-supported prose and the composer adds counts and citations.

severity.description: Concern level in the assessed scope: red for any Critical priority finding or Critical design risk, otherwise yellow for High, otherwise green. Green means no High or Critical concern reported, never production readiness. Refuted findings are excluded; practice findings retain their unproven status.

opening.description: One or two short sentences stating security concerns and consequences in the assessed scope. Lead with the outcome; standard weakness names are allowed. Do not assert production readiness, deployment safety or complete coverage. Do not enumerate findings or severity counts; the composer supplies the counts. No technology identifiers, code, locations or finding IDs.

bullets_intro.description: One short neutral introduction without a ranking or shared access prerequisite. Use Security concerns behind this assessment: on red/yellow, Residual risks worth reviewing: on green. Design risks and unproven findings must not be framed as confirmed attacks.

bullets.description: One to eight evidence-supported scenarios or design concerns. Every red/yellow bullet cites a High or Critical priority finding or design risk. Cite design-risk weaknesses directly when no confirmed finding supports the concern; do not invent an attack.

title.description: Short business-outcome or design-concern headline. Standard weakness names are allowed; implementation details are not.

body.description: Exactly one short sentence in PRODUCT-OWNER language: the weakness class in plain words, optionally followed by its standard term in parentheses, then who can reach it and what an attacker achieves. Describe a business or operational consequence, not an exploit recipe. FORBIDDEN here (they belong in §8/§7): technology identifiers, config keys, library names or version pins, CVE/CWE numbers, file names / paths / file:line refs, framework-internal symbols, port numbers, HTTP-header names, protocol names, code snippets, or backticks. GOOD: 'Missing ownership checks (IDOR) let any signed-in customer read and change another customer's records.' BAD: 'routes/order.ts passes req.params.id to findOne() without an ownerId clause (CWE-639).'

items.description: Live finding F-NNN/T-NNN or design-risk weakness W-NNN. Every reference must directly support the concern and resolve in the current model. The composer displays compact citations; a W reference does not establish confirmed exploitation.

closing.description: ONE short plain-language closing assessment — the bottom line / call to action. Rendered after the bullets blockquote. Do NOT reference F-NNN / T-NNN / W-NNN IDs, security acronyms, attack-class names, config keys, libraries, files, or implementation details.
